drafts.label: @unclebobmartin · gauntlet
drafts.why: Largest builder room; path vs last-frame.
drafts.body:
I get the posture. If you don't read the agent code, the only honest move is that gauntlet — unit tests, gherkin, QA, mutation testing, coverage.

What I’m concerned as a builder: those can all go green while the agent still took a decision you never meant to hand over. High confidence in the last frame is not the same as confidence in the path.

Do your suites also catch wrong intermediate choices, or only that the final metrics look right?

drafts.label: @dieworkwear · homework
drafts.body:
This lands. Secret AI homework makes grade-chasers look fine while people who wanted to learn still do the hard part.

If we only score the finished sheet, causal reasoning never gets pressure-tested — same bug as scoring the last token and never the thinking path.

I personally always prefer assessments that watch how someone arrived, not only whether the homework looks done.

drafts.label: @colebemis · PR screenshots
drafts.body:
This is underrated. Green CI still won’t tell you the UI feels wrong — annotated screenshots force a second look at what actually changed.

I mean it as process evidence, not decoration: the PR stops being “tests passed” and becomes “here is what a human would notice.”

Do you have the agent attach them by default, or only when the diff is visual?

drafts.label: @JensenHuang · open models
drafts.why: Mega first-post room; open + closed both needed.
drafts.body:
Welcome to X — and the letter framing is the right one: the world needs frontier closed models and frontier open models.

What I’m still curious about as a builder: when open models “strengthen safety and cybersecurity,” which checks do we re-run after a release so the community can verify that claim next month, not only trust the announcement?

Sovereignty and diffusion matter. So does a fixed task suite people can actually re-check.

drafts.label: @satyanadella · open-weight
drafts.body:
Open-weight models as essential to a healthy AI ecosystem is the right framing — competitiveness, opportunity, and national security all in one letter.

The part I still want next to that path: can the community re-check behavior with frozen tasks when weights move, not only trust the slide?

Healthy open weights need healthy re-runnable evals too, in my humble opinion.

drafts.label: @SakanaAILabs · benches only
drafts.body:
Respect for shipping Fugu-Ultra v1.1 and putting numbers on the page — up to 7.9 points over v1.0, with ProgramBench and Terminal Bench 2.1 called out.

When a patch moves benches that hard, I personally always prefer a small fixed task list + seeds the community can re-run next week, not only the chart on the announce.

Happy to be wrong if you point to the exact public tasks behind those gains.

drafts.label: @hardmaru · Fable claim
drafts.why: Fable-in-pool claim only on this post.
drafts.tip: Skip if energy low after lab reply — one Fugu room is enough.
drafts.body:
Congrats on the v1.1 ship and the 7.9 point bump.

The line I’m still chewing on is “beating Fable 5 … without even having Fable 5 in our agent pool.” Strong claim — which coding/reasoning suites, and do those tasks stay frozen so outsiders can re-check next week?

I get collective intelligence as the pitch. I personally always prefer that over a one-slide verdict.

drafts.label: @ryanmart3n · Frontier-Bench
drafts.body:
This is the right shape of honesty — 74 tasks, best agents around 34%, and you call it an ongoing community effort instead of a finished leaderboard.

I personally always prefer a hard suite that can still evolve over a saturated bench everyone memorizes.

How should outsiders re-run the same v0.1 tasks next month so “34%” stays comparable when you add more?

drafts.label: @emilkowalski · variants
drafts.why: Passion for learning by trying options — still grounded.
drafts.body:
This is the part of AI that actually feels like learning, not just shipping faster — ask the coding agent for a few variants, switch between them, pass the selection as a query param so a colleague sees the same option.

I’m curious how you decide which variant “wins” though. Is it still pure taste, or do you keep a small checklist so the switcher isn’t only demo candy?

Either way, pairing that with Leva-style controls is a good instinct.

drafts.label: @cb_doge · safety meetings
drafts.why: Ethics: meetings + peer review before release.
drafts.body:
Meetings every few weeks on safety and security risks are better than silence — and peer review of frontier models before public release is the more interesting half of that proposal.

What I’m not totally getting yet: what does “peer review” mean in practice — shared eval suites outsiders can re-run, or closed reviews between labs?

If it’s the first, I personally always prefer that. If it’s only the second, we still have a trust problem.

drafts.label: Short · one original only
drafts.why: Phase 1: single original after 10 replies. Skip if tired.
drafts.body:
Green tests are not a verdict.

An agent can clear the whole gauntlet and still take a decision you never meant to delegate. Same bug as a homework sheet that looks perfect with no thinking underneath.

Score the path. Re-run the same tasks. Last-frame scores will keep lying.
